sections.content: How many people stayed in Kingswinford after gaining qualifications?

Kingswinford is a medium-sized town in the West Midlands. Kingswinford does not have its own university.

Kingswinford has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Kingswinford ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 2,450 state-school pupils from Kingswinford who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 850 (35%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 820 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Kingswinford to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Kingswinford's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Kingswinford in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Kingswinford move to?

Of Kingswinford's graduates, 295 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 100 of those graduates (34%) were living fairly locally, in the Dudley travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Kingswinford's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 255 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 165 of those qualified non-graduates (65%) were living fairly locally, in the Dudley travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Kingswinford's GCSE cohort:

  • 150 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 40 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 17% of graduates and 23% of qualified non-graduates living in Kingswinford had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 660 graduates and 710 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Kingswinford. This is compared with the 850 graduates and 820 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 83% of the graduates had also lived in Kingswinford as GCSE pupils, while 17% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Kingswinford in 2018 to 2019, 78% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 23% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
